paper.title: Learning to Attack: A Bandit Approach to Adversarial Context Poisoning

settings.name_in_paper: Attacker's continuous-armed bandit over attack parameters lambda in [0,1]^3 with contextual state s (GP-UCB)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Guarantee for an attacker (context-poisoning adversary) rather than the learner.
unmapped: Contextual states s are estimated from an IRL surrogate of a non-stationary victim policy; state bias from IRL error and policy drift
Attacker reward r(s,lambda) in RKHS with norm bound B_rkhs, squared-exponential kernel
settings.definition_quote: The attacker's reward function $r(\mathbf{s},\boldsymbol{\lambda})$ lies in the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_k$ with bounded norm $\|r\|_{\mathcal{H}_k} \leq B_{\textsc{rkhs}}$, and observations are corrupted by $\sigma_n$-sub-Gaussian noise.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed contextual bandit victim (R-NeuralUCB) under black-box context poisoning
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Lower bound on regret induced by an attacker (guarantee for the attacker, not the learner).
unmapped: Contexts perturbed by attacker with ||delta||_inf <= epsilon on at most B rounds
Reward h: R^d -> [0,1] is L_h-Lipschitz in the context
settings.definition_quote: The attacker perturbs the context of each arm $i \in [K]$ of the learner, presenting a perturbed context $\tilde{x_{t,i}} = \mathbf{x}_{t,i} + \boldsymbol{\delta}_{t,i}$ with $\|\boldsymbol{\delta}_{t,i}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon$, subject to a total attack budget $B$

algorithms.name: AdvBandit (GP-UCB attack parameter selection with MaxEnt IRL surrogate and PGD)

symbols.n_att: number of attack rounds n (n <= B)
symbols.gamma_T: maximum information gain gamma_n at n_att, O((log n)^(d_gp+1)) for SE kernel
symbols.d_Theta: number of IRL parameters, O(d d_h K)
symbols.eps_mis: misspecification error of the IRL model class (TV)

conditions: attacker reward in RKHS with bounded norm, sigma_n-sub-Gaussian noise, SE kernel
victim R-NeuralUCB with O(1/sqrt t) exploration bonus

source.label: thm:attacker_regret_full
source.quote: Let $\boldsymbol{\lambda}^*(\mathbf{s}) = \arg\max_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}} r(\mathbf{s},\boldsymbol{\lambda})$. Under Assumption~\ref{assm:approx_real}, with probability at least $1-\rho$, the attacker's cumulative regret over $n$ attack rounds satisfies: R_{attack}(n) \le O(\sqrt{n \gamma_n \log(n/\rho)}) + O(\sqrt{n} \sqrt{d_\Theta/W}) + O(\sqrt{n \Delta_{IRL}}) + n \epsilon_{mis}.

results.notes: Out-of-scope attacker guarantee. Regret measured against per-state optimal lambda*(s).

symbols.gamma_T: maximum information gain gamma_n at n_att

conditions: W = Omega(d_Theta) and constant Delta_IRL (from proof)

source.label: thm:attacker_regret_full
source.quote: Under exact realizability ($\epsilon_{\text{mis}} = 0$), this simplifies to $R_{\text{attack}}(n) \leq O(\sqrt{n \gamma_n \log(n/\rho)} + \sqrt{n})$.

results.notes: Special case of r1 stated in the theorem.

bound.expression_latex: R_v(T) \geq B \bar{\alpha} - O(\sqrt{B}\sqrt{d_\Theta/W}) - O(\sqrt{B \Delta_{IRL}}) - O(\sqrt{T\log T})

symbols.alpha_bar: average positive attackability margin (1/B) sum [Delta(x_t,a_t^dagger) - 2 L_h epsilon]^+

conditions: victim is R-NeuralUCB with O(sqrt T) unattacked regret
attacker is AdvBandit with budget B and perturbation bound epsilon
h maps to [0,1] and is L_h-Lipschitz

source.label: thm:victim_regret
source.quote: With attack budget $B$, perturbation bound $\epsilon$, and IRL retraining interval $\Delta_{\textsc{irl}}$ with window size $W$, the victim's cumulative regret satisfies with probability at least $1-\rho$: R_v(T) \geq B \bar{\alpha} - O(\sqrt{B}\sqrt{d_\Theta/W}) - O(\sqrt{B \Delta_{IRL}}) - O(\sqrt{T \log T}).

results.notes: Lower bound on victim regret induced by a specific attacker against a specific victim; subtracted terms are O(.) so Omega notation is an approximation of the stated form.
